speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe when the itching started and if you’ve noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes? Also, have you had any recent changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I am concerned about primary sclerosing cholangitis. Do you notice any darkening of your urine or pale, clay-colored stools?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of scleral icterus confirms jaundice, and your history of ulcerative colitis strongly points toward cholestatic liver disease. I need to rule out other causes like viral hepatitis or autoimmune hepatitis, so I will order specific blood work. REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests, Viral Hepatitis Panel, Anti-Mitochondrial Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: The markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase with only mild transaminase elevation confirms a cholestatic pattern, and the negative AMA makes primary biliary cholangitis unlikely. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I suspect primary sclerosing cholangitis, so I need to visualize the bile ducts. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is normal, I must rule out extrahepatic causes of cholestasis such as malignancy or stones. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilatation strongly support a diagnosis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, despite the initial normal MRCP reading, which can occasionally miss small-duct disease. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, this association is classic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
